data.one_liner: Fast, low-memory library for reading, creating, editing, and styling Excel files.
data.what_it_does: Reads, creates, edits, and styles Microsoft Excel spreadsheets (.xlsx) and legacy .xls files. Provides features like formulas, charts, pivot tables, CSV import/export, and JSON export in Dart and Flutter.
use_when: You need to read, write, or modify Excel (.xlsx or .xls) spreadsheets in Dart or Flutter
You are processing large workbooks and require low memory consumption and streaming parsers
You want a drop-in, faster replacement for the existing excel package
avoid_when: You only need simple CSV handling and do not require Excel-specific features or formatting
You are working entirely within a native environment that already handles spreadsheet binding seamlessly
strengths: Significantly faster encode and decode times and lower peak memory usage compared to the legacy excel package
Supports legacy .xls workbooks alongside modern .xlsx files without extra dependencies
Rich feature set covering formulas, charts, pivot tables, styling, conditional formatting, and CSV/JSON conversion
Cross-platform support across Dart VM, Flutter mobile, and Web (JS & WASM)
weaknesses: Formulas are written in A1 notation; R1C1 notation is not natively used for writing formulas
Conflicting dependency majors mean it cannot run alongside the original excel package in the same program
